intro.title: Build your resume from scratch.
intro.subtitle: We walk you through it, one section at a time.
intro.p1: This takes 15-20 minutes if you do it right. That's not a lot of time to invest in something this important. But it only works if you take it seriously.
intro.p2: We go section by section: contact info, work history, skills, education. Answer each question in your own words. Don't try to make it sound fancy. Just tell us what's true.
intro.gapsBody: You might have gaps in your history because of incarceration, family obligations, health, or anything else. You don't need to hide or explain them here. Just include what you have. The Forge helps you figure out how to talk about the gaps later, on your terms.

name.title: What's your full name?
name.subtitle: This goes at the top of your resume.

contact.title: Contact information
contact.subtitle: Goes on your resume. Add what you have. It's all optional.

job.subtitleFirst: The last job you held. Full-time, part-time, temp, gig, or work program. All count.
job.subtitleNth: Same as before: title, company, and when.
job.companyPlaceholder: e.g., Amazon, City of Milwaukee, Self-employed

duties.title: What did you do there?
duties.subtitle: Main responsibilities in your own words. Don't make it fancy. Just be honest.
duties.footer: Include accomplishments, things you were proud of, skills you used.
duties.placeholder: e.g., Operated forklift and pallet jack. Helped train 3 new employees on safety. Maintained 99% on-time order rate during peak season.
duties.attention: One number beats a paragraph here. How many, how often, how big. Whatever you actually remember.

more.title: Do you have another job to add?
more.subtitle: More work history makes a stronger resume. Part-time, temp, and gig work all count.
more.count: {count, plural, =1 {# job added so far.} other {# jobs added so far.}}
more.yesBody: Full-time, part-time, temp, gig work, or work program

skills.title: What are your skills and certifications?
skills.subtitle: What are you good at? Technical skills, people skills, physical skills, licenses. Everything counts.
skills.placeholder: e.g., Forklift certified (OSHA), CDL Class A, Microsoft Excel, bilingual English/Spanish, team leadership, conflict de-escalation

education.title: Education and training
education.subtitle: School, GED, trade programs, certifications, military. They all count. Include anything you completed, even programs from inside.
education.placeholder: e.g., GED (2018), HVAC certification (ABC Training, 2020), OSHA 10-hour safety, US Army 2004-2008

extras.title: Anything else?
extras.subtitle: Volunteer work, community roles, programs you've been part of, or anything that doesn't fit above.
extras.placeholder: e.g., Volunteer at Milwaukee Rescue Mission 2023-present, peer mentor in reentry program, completed financial literacy and conflict resolution

review.title: Here's what we have.
review.subtitle: Review before we start the analysis. Go back to fix anything.
review.note: This is the raw material for the Forge analysis. The AI transforms it into a structured career narrative. You'll see the full output at the end.

paste.title: Paste your resume
paste.subtitle: Copy your resume text from anywhere and paste it below. Don't worry about formatting.
paste.minimum: Minimum 20 characters. Just get the basics in there.
paste.aiHelp: Already use ChatGPT or another AI? Have it write your resume, then paste it here.
paste.aiHelpNote: Copy this prompt, give it to your AI, then paste its answer in the box below. We handle the formatting.
paste.aiPrompt: Please write out my resume as plain text. Include my name, phone, email, and city. List every job I have held with the employer name, dates, and 2-4 bullet points describing what I actually did. Then list my skills and any education, certificates, or training. Do not invent anything. Only use what you know about me from our conversations or what I tell you now. Ask me questions first if you need more detail.
paste.placeholder:
Paste your resume here...

Example:
John Smith
Forklift Operator with 5 years experience

Work History:
Warehouse Associate, Amazon, 2019-2024
- Operated forklift and pallet jack
- Trained new team members
paste.keepGoing: Keep going. We need a little more to work with.

builder.title: Here's your resume. Let's make it strong.
builder.intro: We organized what you gave us. Check every section and fix anything that's off. It's all yours to edit. This becomes your base resume: the one we aim at specific jobs later.
builder.weakTitle: A few lines could be stronger.
builder.weakBody: The best resumes show what you did, with real numbers. Tap Strengthen with help under any bullet. We ask a few questions and turn your answer into a strong line. We only ever use what you tell us.
builder.fullLater: The full version comes after the next steps, and it is stronger.
builder.beforeNote: This is the before version. If you need a copy today (an appointment, a program requirement), grab one, then come back and finish.
builder.txtTitle: Plain text is the safest format for online application boxes
builder.readinessTitle: Before you go: are you ready to use this?
builder.readinessNote: A gut check, and nothing here is scored. The resume is half of it; owning it is the other half.

readiness.explain: I can explain every bullet on this resume out loud.
readiness.story: I have a real story behind my strongest experience.
readiness.fit: I know why this resume fits the jobs I'm going for.
readiness.next: I know my next step (apply, gather proof, or pick a better-fit role).

sync.question: There's a resume in progress on this computer. Is it yours?
sync.note: Nothing in it is used until you answer. If it isn't yours, we erase it from this computer.
sync.yesAccount: Yes, save it to my account
sync.saved: Your work so far is saved to your account.
sync.failed: We couldn't save your work to your account yet. It's still on this computer, and we'll try again.
